claims.explanation: SB-590885 is a selective BRAF inhibitor whose cytotoxicity depends on oncogenic BRAF-driven MAPK signaling; cell lines harboring activating BRAF mutations (especially V600E) are sensitized, while resistance arises through RAF isoform switching, IGF-1R/PI3K activation, or upstream RAS/RTK alterations that bypass BRAF dependence. The virtual-cell signature showing downregulation of MAPK feedback genes DUSP4/DUSP6/FOSL1 and similarity to a MEK inhibitor supports on-pathway MAPK inhibition as the selective mechanism.

features.basis: Oncogenic BRAF alleles confer selective sensitivity to SB-590885 (PMID 17145850)
RAS-driven RAF isoform switching/feedback bypasses BRAF-selective inhibition
Enhanced IGF-1R/PI3K signaling mediates acquired BRAF-inhibitor resistance
MEK mutations can activate ERK downstream of RAF, bypassing BRAF inhibition
MEK2 F57C is less RAF-dependent and resistant to RAF inhibition
Flexible switching among RAF isoforms underlies resistance to BRAF inhibitors
Virtual-cell downregulation of MAPK feedback phosphatases indicates on-pathway BRAF/MEK inhibition
MAPK-dependent AP-1 component downregulated by SB-590885 in responsive lines
MYC downregulation in HT29 virtual-cell response reflects MAPK pathway blockade
RTK/PI3K upregulation can bypass BRAF dependence and drive resistance
